dedupe_keys.name: quebec rural emergency 360 a mixed methods study of barriers and priorities in all 26 rural emergency departments

description: This case study documents the characteristics, problems and improvement priorities of every rural emergency department in the province of Québec, Canada, after reforms to health governance, funding and service delivery changed how they operate. Richard Fleet and colleagues from Université Laval, Université de Montréal, the Université du Québec à Montréal and regional health and social services centres published it in PLOS ONE in September 2026. The participatory mixed-methods design covered 26 rural emergency departments and combined administrative statistics, structured site surveys, semi-structured interviews with stakeholders and a validation survey of local champions, analysed by triangulation and cross-cutting thematic analysis. The article is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is provincial. Caveats: the interview material is qualitative and the administrative statistics are not released with the article. Four themes emerged, namely governance, organisation of care, access to resources and professional practice; participants reported reduced local autonomy, administrative complexity and budget models poorly suited to rural settings, and asked for standardised but locally flexible processes, regional emergency service managers and rural-sensitive performance measures. Simulation uses: constraints and priorities of small emergency departments for regional access and service configuration models. Related records: the Québec emergency department indicators by facility (data-quebec-emergency-department-data) give the matching administrative series.
